newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals recover to close higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals recover to close higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures recovered from early weakness to close higher Tuesday, as funds covered short positions in gold, and Russian supply disruptions continued to provide support for platinum group metals (PGMs).
"Gold prices have now built a base around $340 an ounce this year, with lower prices clearly attracting physical demand," Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt said.
"Plus the talk of a Federal Reserve monetary policy tightening cycle, and a healthy U.S. economy, is probably reminding people of the potential for inflation."
COMEX June gold ended up $1.80 an ounce at $350.50, the first close above $350 since April 10, after finding support around $348.00 following a weaker opening.
COMEX gold open interest fell a further 1,1916 lots Monday to 161,442 lots, reflecting fund shortcovering, analysts said.

"With the technical indicators turning positive, and a large net short speculative position being held by funds, according to the latest CFTC data, there's the potential for a rally based on fund shortcovering alone," Platt said.
COMEX June gold's five-day moving-average crossed back above its 20-day moving average this week, and the contract is now testing resistance around its 50-day average.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $349.25/75, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $348.90 an ounce, and the New York close Monday around $347.40/90.
After seeing a four year low around $337.00 in January, spot gold prices found support again in the past few weeks around $340 an ounce, and recovered to four week highs Monday.

The main change in economic fundamentals in the past week has been the sharp slide in the U.S. dollar, which fell to three months lows against the yen around 118 yen, making precious metals cheaper for investors and fabricators in yen terms, analysts said. Only last month dollar/yen had reached four year highs around 127 yen.
COMEX July silver closed up 4.3 cents at $4.878 an ounce, after finding support quickly around $4.820 early in the day.

Silver was more likely to be traded from the long side by the funds, as the gap between mine supply and fabrication demand was continuing to widen, drawing down inventories, and central banks sales were not hanging over the market, as they are in the gold market, analysts said.
Like gold, physical offtake of silver in the Far East, particularly India, was also robust, as de-regulation and a series of good monsoons was boosting disposable income, analysts said.
NYMEX July platinum ended up 80 cents at $391.90 an ounce, after recovering from early weakness, and after seeing 10-week highs Monday.
The October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread widened further to new highs for the two contracts at $39.70 an ounce.
NYMEX June palladium also recovered from a weak opening to see a new contract high at $174.75 an ounce, before ending down 30 cents at $171.55.
The June/September palladium spread went further into backwardation at $3.10 an ounce, while December palladium saw new contract highs at $172.50 an ounce.
Overnight Russia's metal export agency confirmed it was in talks with customers over the resumption of supply contracts for PGM's and said exports should resume again in June.

But after five months of disruption to Russian PGM exports, it would take some time for confidence in the supply line to be restored, meaning there was going to be good demand for Russian exports to rebuild inventories, keeping prices high, analysts said.

"In the meantime, fabricators need the metal now and auto industry demand is growing for palladium in particular, forcing some dealers to pay over 20 percent to borrow the metal to meet commitments," one refining source said.
